messages:
Maya: Quick sync — want to align on Q3+ roadmap for cross-region resilience and the customer onramp acceptance criteria. Focus areas: traffic steering semantics, eviction behavior during regional degradation, and what we call a 'resilience contract' vs our baseline SLA. Who's got bandwidth to help define launch gates?
Arjun: I can help. Do we have an ordered list of customer asks? I remember 3 big ones: deterministic latency, predictable failover, and data residency for a few accounts.
Elaine: Correct. From CS: two fintech customers want explicit failover SLAs + dry-run cutovers. A couple of startups just want guidance/recipes for multi-region staging.
Priya: From infra constraints: we can offer fast failover if we keep warm standbys or route-level replicas, but cost jumps. Need to map cost delta to customer tiers.
Dan: SRE note: we also need clear evacuation behavior. If a region degrades, do we throttle, queue, or evict best-effort tenants? That determines rollout criteria.
Maya: Agreed. Proposal: define 3 onramp paths — Sandbox Guidance (self-serve), Standard Resilience (auto-routing + soft-evict), and Resilience Contract (dedicated capacity + guaranteed cross-region fallback). Thoughts?
Arjun: +1 to three paths. For Standard Resilience, we should document routing precedence: local -> regional fallback -> global fallback, with quick config toggles. Keep fallbacks non-destructive (no eviction) unless latency SLOs violated.
Priya: Implementation sketch (short):
```
- Routing tiers: LOCAL / NEAR_REGIONAL / GLOBAL
- Fallback policy: try NEAR_REGIONAL within 200ms, else GLOBAL within 500ms
- Eviction threshold: only evict when queue>5000 and p50 latency > 2s for >30s
- Warm-standby: optional, billed as premium for Resilience Contract
```
Dan: Need telemetry hooks for each step (routing decision, failover reason, evict reason). Also set alerting: page SRE on repeated GLOBAL failovers for >3mins.
Elaine: For customer cutover acceptance — CS requires a dry-run checklist: 1) simulated failover, 2) latency delta report, 3) rollout rollback plan, 4) data residency verification. If those pass, customers sign Resilience Contract.
Maya: Nice. Can we convert Priya's sketch + Elaine's checklist into a launch acceptance doc? Also prioritize which customers to pilot in Q3.
Arjun: Suggest pilot candidates: "Atlas Fin" (needs hard SLA), "QuickForms" (wants guidance), and internal staging for infra validation. We should run end-to-end dry-run with Atlas Fin first.
Priya: I'll estimate infra delta for warm-standby per region and itemize cost. ETA EOW.
Dan: I'll stub telemetry dashboard and add alerts to the runbook. ETA next Wed.
Elaine: I'll coordinate with Atlas Fin legal on resilience contract terms and schedule a dry-run window.
Maya: Great — action items: Priya (cost delta + infra checklist), Dan (telemetry + alerts), Elaine (customer scheduling + contract draft), Arjun (pilot plan + failure-mode tests). I'll add this to the product roadmap board and mark it as a high-priority cross-team initiative. Please add any blockers in the card.
deploy-bot: test-run created for pilot: job/1764567891-pilot-dryrun queued — ETA 48h. :robot_face:
Arjun: Thanks, team. One more ask — include a short blurb for sales describing tiers & pricing impact so revenue ops can prep offers.
Maya: Will do, adding sales blurb to the roadmap card. If nobody objects, we'll treat this as the canonical onramp model and iterate after pilot feedback. :thumbsup:
